_metadata.description: Determinations that exist as prose in an opinion or a regulation rather than as a column in any export, and so can only arrive by hand. Three kinds appear here: a market withdrawing an authorisation, a regulator requiring a warning on the label, and a health body finding that real intake exceeds its own guidance value. That last one is the reason the file exists — the corpus holds hundreds of acceptable daily intakes and, deliberately, rates none of them, because an ADI is the output of a safety assessment. An authority concluding that people actually exceed one is a different statement, and it is the only thing that should move a level. REVIEW STATUS: ai_seeded. Every regulation, opinion and date named here is real and the determinations are accurately represented, but the statements are not verbatim extracts and carry no URL, because a guessed link is worse than none. Replacing them with quoted text from the published documents is a curation task, not a code change.

records.statement: Removed from the EU list of permitted food additives. EFSA concluded in May 2021 that titanium dioxide (E 171) can no longer be considered safe when used as a food additive, because a concern for genotoxicity could not be ruled out and no acceptable daily intake could therefore be established. Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/63 deleted E 171 from the Union list, with the prohibition applying from August 2022 after a transition period.

citation.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/63 amending Annexes II and III to Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 as regards the food additive titanium dioxide (E 171)

records.threshold: 0.07 mg nitrite ion per kg of body weight per day
records.statement: EFSA set an acceptable daily intake for nitrite of 0.07 mg nitrite ion per kg of body weight per day in its 2017 re-evaluation of nitrites as food additives, and found that this intake was exceeded — by children at the higher end of consumption from the additive use alone, and across several age groups once all dietary sources of nitrite were counted together.

citation.title: Re-evaluation of potassium nitrite (E 249) and sodium nitrite (E 250) as food additives

records.warningText: may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children
records.statement: Foods containing this colour must carry the warning "may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children" under Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008. The requirement covers six colours — E 102, E 104, E 110, E 122, E 124 and E 129 — and followed the Southampton study on colours and hyperactivity in children.

citation.title: Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 on food additives, Annex V
